title: Notes Java Introduction To Control Constructs

runs.text: 1. What are control constructs in Java?
Control constructs are statements used to control the flow of execution in a Java program according to a requirement or condition.
By default, Java executes statements sequentially. Control constructs allow us to change this flow by:
Executing selected statements
Skipping statements
Executing one block out of multiple blocks
Repeating statements
Jumping out of a control structure
2. Why do we need control constructs?
Control constructs are required because every program does not need to execute all statements in a linear order.
For example:
Some statements may need to be skipped.
Only one statement out of two may need to be executed.
One block may need to be executed based on a condition.
Different statements may need to execute multiple times.
Control may need to move directly to another part of the program.
Therefore, control constructs help us execute a program according to the situation and requirement.
3. What is linear or sequential execution?
Linear or sequential execution means that the statements of a program are executed one after another in the same order in which they are written.

4. Explain the execution flow of a simple Java program.
When a Java program is executed:
The JVM starts the program.
The JVM calls the
main(
) method.
Control enters the
main(

The first statement is executed.
Control moves to the next statement.
Each statement is executed sequentially.
When the closing brace of the method is reached, control returns to the JVM.
This is called sequential or linear execution.

A simple if statement works as follows:
If the condition is true, the statement or block inside the if is executed.
If the condition is false, the statement or block inside the if is skipped.
After that, control continues with the next statement after the if block.

16. What is an if-else statement?
An if-else statement is a conditional control construct used when exactly one of two statements or blocks of statements must be executed.

17. How does an if-else statement work?
An if-else statement works as follows:

If the condition is false, the else block is executed.

runs.text: 22. What is an else-if ladder?
An else-if ladder is a conditional control construct used when there are multiple conditions and multiple possible blocks of statements.
The conditions are checked one by one. When a condition becomes true, its block is executed, and the remaining conditions are skipped.
Syntax:
23. When should we use an else-if ladder?
An else-if ladder should be used when:
There are more than two possible conditions.
Multiple blocks are available.
Only one block should be executed at a given point in time.
The selected block depends on the value or condition.
24. How does an else-if ladder execute?
The execution of an else-if ladder follows these steps:
The first condition is checked.
If it is true, its block is executed.
The remaining conditions are skipped.
If the first condition is false, the next condition is checked.
This continues until a true condition is found.
If no condition is true, the else block is executed, if present.
25. What is the purpose of the final else block in an else-if ladder?
The final else block is used to handle all values that do not satisfy any of the previous conditions.
It acts as the default block.
Example:
If the number is not 1, 2, or 3, the else block is executed.
26. How can we display the day based on a number using an else-if ladder?
Output:
Tuesday
Only the block associated with number == 3 is executed.
27. What is the disadvantage of using a long else-if ladder?
In an else-if ladder, conditions are checked one after another.
For example, if there are 100 conditions and the last condition is true, the program may need to check many previous conditions before reaching the last one.
Therefore:
Multiple comparisons may be required.
The code becomes lengthy.
It may be less efficient when many conditions compare the same variable with fixed values.
The code may become difficult to maintain.
28. What is a switch statement?
A switch statement is a conditional control construct used to select one block of code from multiple possible cases based on the value of an expression.
Syntax:
29. When should we use a switch statement?
A switch statement should be used when:
There are multiple possible values.
The value of one expression determines which block should execute.
Only one case should normally execute.
The same variable is compared against several fixed values.
For example, selecting a day based on a number is suitable for a switch statement.
30. How does a switch statement work?
A switch statement works as follows:
The expression is evaluated.
The result is compared with the case values.
Control moves directly to the matching case.
The statements inside that case are executed.
The break statement exits the switch.
If no case matches, the default block is executed.
31. How can we display the day using a switch statement?
Output:
Tuesday
The value 3 matches case 3, so Tuesday is printed.
32. What is the purpose of the case label in a switch statement?
The case label represents a possible value of the switch expression.
Example:
If the switch expression is equal to 1, control moves to this case.
33. What is the purpose of the default block in a switch statement?
The default block is executed when none of the case values matches the switch expression.
Example:
If number is 8, the output will be:
Invalid number
34. What happens if the break statement is not used in a switch case?
If break is not used, control does not stop after executing the matching case.
Instead, control continues executing the statements of the following cases. This
behavior
is called fall-through.
Example:
Output:
Monday
Tuesday
Invalid day
The switch starts execution from case 2 and continues into the following cases because there are no break statements.
35. What is fall-through in a switch statement?
Fall-through is the
behavior
in which control continues executing the next case statements after a matching case because a break statement is missing.
For example, if case 4 matches and there is no break, the statements in cases 5, 6, and 7 may also execute.
36. What is the purpose of the break statement?
The main purpose of the break statement is to bring control out of the current control construct.
In a switch statement, break:
Stops execution of the current case.
Prevents execution of the following cases.
Transfers control outside the switch statement.
37. How does break work in a switch statement?
When the matching case is executed, the break statement immediately brings control outside the switch.

In the discussed example, the else-if ladder checks conditions one by one.

What is the main difference between break, continue, and return?
The break statement brings control completely out of the current control construct.
The continue statement skips the remaining statements of the current loop iteration and moves to the next iteration of the loop.
The return statement exits from the current method and returns control to the calling method.
